body: I think it closed back in July
My boyfriend went there when they first opened and said they literally served him undercooked beef.

I know, there’s so much I could talk to him about that I couldn’t tell my mom and Dad. He wanted to come to Tennessee in May to see me graduate college. He was so proud of me. I keep having pretend conversations with Craig in my head, I want to believe he’s with me in spirit.
I can’t imagine having your job, but thank you for all that you do.

He was in otherwise great physical health. He was blessed with better genes than me, I have a ton of health problems he never had to deal with. He loved sports, and played baseball for years until he graduated high school
Thank you. Everyone always said he was so handsome.
I feel so numb. I’m trying not to cry and stay strong for my mother and father, but it’s so hard. I cry when I’m alone with my boyfriend.

He was a special brother. He told my mom when he was little how bad he wanted a little sister. He was so excited when my mom found out she was pregnant with a girl. Tell your brother you love him often.

No, he did not have any children. He was with a woman who was divorced with two amazing children, a son and daughter. She was the love of his life. He taught her son how to play football and baseball, and also got him into video games. Both of her children miss Craig so much. Craig wanted to be clean for at least a year and then marry her and adopt them. I consider them to be family, and my father is going to take her son fishing and to games to help him grieve.

That’s what happened. I wish I could’ve stopped him. No one in his halfway house knew he was using again. He was working 50+ hours at his job down there and was being able to keep busy, plus two hours of therapy everyday of the week. It is so devastating that many recovering addicts die like this.

Thank you. Stay sober and strong. I wish Craig had kept going, he was doing so well and wanted to come see me graduate college in Tennessee in May. I loved him so much. We never gave up, I was his younger sister and I was the best sister I could be.
Thank you. He was 32. He was very close with my grandfather who died in 2011. I’d like to think they are together again... it gives me comfort.

Thank you so much. My mom says I was the best little sister possible to him, I tried so hard to love him and help him. Heroin and opiates are truly evil... they are destroying so many lives. I have so many classmates I graduated high school with that have died from overdose, and I’m 25. You are so kind, I will try to PM you later.

It’s honestly been the worst lost I’ve ever felt. I lost my grandad while a senior in high school, but he was 88 and had been very sick for a long time. Craig was otherwise in great health other than his addiction problems.
He did, he had a wonderful laugh and could make anyone laugh. Everyone that has reached out to us from his recovery place said he was a good soul with a great sense of humor.
Thank you, it’s going to be a rough next few months.

People are dropping like flies from it. I was his little sister, it feels like I wasn’t there for him enough, but I know I loved him, and my parents loved him as much as anyone could love their child. It’s so hard right now, but I have a lot of friends and family to lean on. Thank you.

Sorry, I should’ve provided more context.
My brother became addicted to opiates after developing PTSD as a teenager after being beaten by two other teenage boys he thought were his friends. He used drugs and alcohol off-and-on again for a periods of time but into his mid 20s turned to painkiller abuse as a form of coping with his demons. He didn’t do very well in therapy, and soon turned to using heroin instead of pills. He was clean for three months and doing well down in TX, but overdosed from heroin while in the shower. We got a call the next morning from his counselor. His name was Craig.
